jobs.department: Isle of Man Financial Services Authority
jobs.location: Finch Hill House (Isle of Man Financial Services Authority)
jobs.fullDescription:
Job Reference:
IOMF-025658
Salary:
£38,500 - £63,500
Closing Date:
22/10/2026
Department:
Isle of Man Financial Services Authority
Location:
Finch Hill House (Isle of Man Financial Services Authority)
Employment Type:
Permanent
Hours Per Week:
37
Job Advert
The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (“the Authority”) regulates firms engaged in financial activities, including insurance, pensions, banking, investments, fiduciary services, and fund administration. The Authority is also responsible for oversight of anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance for those involved in the financial sector as well as a range of other Designated Businesses and has oversight of compliance with the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017.
MANAGER – BANKING (PRUDENTIAL SUPERVISION)
An opportunity has arisen at the Authority for the role of Manager – Banking in the Prudential Supervision Division.
This is a unique opportunity to play a key role in the supervision and development of one of the Isle of Man's most important financial sectors. As part of a highly skilled and collaborative team, you will contribute to the oversight of the Island’s diverse banking sector which holds £45 billion of deposits and provides £11 billion of lending.
About the role
Working at the heart of prudential and conduct regulation, you will engage with industry leaders, other international regulators, assess business models and risk frameworks, and support the Authority's regulatory objectives to maintain a strong, stable and internationally respected financial services sector.
You will have the opportunity to influence supervisory approaches, contribute to policy development and provide expert insight into emerging risks within the banking sector.
About you
You will bring extensive relevant banking, or equivalent industry experience in an operational, compliance, assurance, risk or audit role, together with a strong understanding of the financial services sector and the associated legislation, regulation and guidance.
You will also demonstrate:
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills;
The ability to interpret and communicate complex information clearly and effectively;
Sound judgement and a pragmatic approach to problem-solving;
A flexible and collaborative working style;
A commitment to continuous professional development.
A professional qualification relevant to the financial services industry is desirable, or you should be willing to work towards obtaining one.
Why join the Authority?
In return, you’ll have the opportunity to:
Contribute to the development of the Isle of Man’s financial system, particularly the banking sector;
Play an important role in the delivery of the Authority’s diverse and important mandate;
Assist with the delivery of strategically important supervision work as part of a highly professional team;
Build a fulfilling career, reaching your full potential and feeling valued in an environment that supports diversity and inclusion;
Be part of a dynamic team where no two days are the same.
What we offer
This is an exceptional opportunity within a people focused organisation and applicants seeking flexible working arrangements are welcome.
Our package includes:
Competitive salary
Defined benefit pension
Support for professional studies
25 days annual leave
Flexible working scheme
For a full job description and to apply please see the attachments linked below.
Closing date for applications is 22 October 2026
The Authority is an equal opportunities employer.

Job Advert
The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (“the Authority”) is the regulatory body for the financial sector in the Isle of Man and regulates firms engaged in a range of financial activities, including insurance, pensions, banking, fiduciary services, fund administration and management and investment advice and management. The Authority is responsible for oversight of anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance for those involved in the financial sector and a range of other Designated Businesses, and has oversight of compliance with the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017.
SENIOR MANAGER – PORTFOLIO SUPERVISION
An exciting opportunity has arisen to join the Authority’s Portfolio Supervision Division as a Senior Manager – Portfolio Supervision.
Working as part of the Division’s Senior Management Team, the successful candidate will play a leading role in the development, consultation, stakeholder engagement and implementation of reforms to the Island’s pensions regulatory framework, including work associated with the Retirement Benefits Schemes (Amendment) Bill. A significant element of the role will involve engaging with industry participants, professional advisers, representative bodies, Government departments and other stakeholders to help shape and implement the Authority’s future approach to pensions regulation and supervision.
The successful candidate will also oversee the effective and efficient supervision of regulated and registered firms and individuals within the Division’s portfolio and contribute as a member of the Authority’s Senior Management Team to the delivery of the Authority’s strategic objectives.
We are seeking an experienced pensions professional with significant experience working within, supervising or advising participants in the pensions sector, including retirement benefits schemes, pension administration and associated regulatory frameworks. The successful candidate will have proven leadership experience and the credibility, communication skills and stakeholder engagement capabilities required to represent the Authority effectively across a wide range of industry and public sector forums.
Applicants should possess a strong understanding of pensions legislation, regulation and industry practice, together with the ability to analyse complex issues, manage competing priorities and contribute to the successful delivery of a major programme of regulatory reform. A relevant professional qualification is essential.
This is a unique opportunity to help shape the future pensions regulatory framework in the Isle of Man while contributing to the Authority’s wider supervisory and strategic objectives.
The right candidate will bring the above skills and experience to the role. In return, working at the Authority will provide the successful candidate with the opportunity to:
contribute directly to the development and implementation of the Island’s pensions regulatory framework;
play an important role in the delivery of the Authority’s regulatory objectives and strategic priorities;
work closely with industry, Government, professional advisers and other key stakeholders;
provide leadership within the Portfolio Supervision Division and contribute as a member of the Authority’s Senior Management Team;
assist with the delivery of strategically important legislative, policy and supervisory work; and
build a fulfilling career in a collaborative and inclusive environment that supports professional development.
The role is full-time, working 37 hours per week.
Our package includes:
Competitive salary
Defined benefit pension
Support for professional studies
25 days annual leave
Flexible working

Closing date for applications is 21 October 2026.

Job Advert
About the role
We are looking for a qualified and enthusiastic Clinical Scientist or Clinical Physiologist with expertise in Cardiac Rhythm Management to join our Cardiorespiratory Team within Manx Care on the Isle of Man.
This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in delivering and developing Cardiac Rhythm Management services for the Island's population while furthering your own professional development within a supportive and progressive healthcare environment.
Working as part of our specialist Cardiorespiratory Team, you will be responsible to the Cardiorespiratory Manager and collaborate closely with experienced colleagues across the service to provide high-quality, patient-centred care. You will support the delivery of a responsive, efficient and cost-effective diagnostic service while contributing to ongoing service improvement and development.
The post is offered at Band 7 for applicants who hold professional registration as a Clinical Scientist or Clinical Physiologist together with certification in Cardiac Rhythm Management (IBHRE, BHRS or equivalent).
You will provide a high-quality, accurate and quality-assured Cardiac Rhythm Management service, ensuring diagnostic standards, service requirements and turnaround times are consistently met. You will also contribute to the ongoing development of the service and support the delivery of excellent care for patients across the Island.
Help shape the future of Cardiorespiratory Services
Noble's Hospital is recruiting a number of Cardiorespiratory Physiologists to join our expanding department. These opportunities form part of a planned investment in the future of our service and offer the chance to play an important role in its continued development.
Why are we recruiting multiple roles?
Our Cardiorespiratory Department has a long-standing reputation for delivering outstanding patient care. As part of our workforce planning strategy, we are strengthening the team to support:
Sustainable service delivery for the future
Knowledge sharing from highly experienced senior staff
Continuity of expertise across cardiac, respiratory and sleep services
Service development and innovation in line with modern healthcare needs
With several senior team members approaching retirement over the coming years, we are recruiting proactively to allow time for structured training, mentorship and succession planning. This approach helps safeguard specialist knowledge, supports professional development and ensures patients continue to receive a seamless, high-quality service.
About the Department
The Cardiorespiratory Department at Noble’s Hospital provides a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic services, including:
Cardiac rhythm management
Echocardiography
Non-invasive cardiac diagnostics
Respiratory diagnostics
Sleep and ventilation services
You will join a close-knit and supportive multidisciplinary team that works closely with consultants, nursing colleagues and allied health professionals to deliver high-quality care for the Island's population.

Job Advert
The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (“the Authority”) regulates firms engaged in financial activities, including insurance, pensions, banking, investments, fiduciary services, and fund administration. The Authority is also responsible for oversight of anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) compliance for those involved in the financial sector as well as a range of other Designated Businesses and has oversight of compliance with the Beneficial Ownership Act 2017.
PORTFOLIO SUPERVISION DIVISION – VACANCIES
The Authority is seeking to fill a number of vacancies within the Portfolio Supervision Division. This is an exciting time to join the Authority to help us deliver our objectives which include an updated approach to supervision and oversight, enhanced data management and analytics and the reduction of financial crime. The successful candidates will join an existing Division who are responsible for the efficient supervision of firms across the finance sectors. The successful candidates will be enthusiastic team players who can demonstrate some of the following attributes:
At Assistant Manager level:
Relevant finance sector industry experience in an operational, compliance, assurance, risk or audit role.
Holds, or is working towards, a professional qualification relevant to the financial services industry.
A working knowledge of Financial Services and associated legislation, regulation, and guidance.
Proven ability to build and maintain working relationships with both internal and external stakeholders at all levels including the ability to influence and negotiate.
Ability to prepare and actively participate in meetings with senior stakeholders both internally and externally.
At Supervision Officer level:
An interest in, and working knowledge of, Financial Services and associated legislation, regulation and guidance.
Strong organisational skills, including accuracy, attention to detail and record keeping.
Effective interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.
These are exceptional opportunities within a people focused organisation and applicants seeking flexible working arrangements are welcome.
Our package includes:
Competitive salary
Defined benefit pension
Support for professional studies
25 days annual leave
Flexible working scheme

Closing date for applications is 9 October 2026

Promote recovery, independence, relapse prevention, and social inclusion.
Maintain accurate electronic records and discharge-related documentation.

We are searching for a Senior Youth Worker with the skills and enthusiasm to shape practice, lead meaningful change and make a real difference for young people across the Isle of Man.
We are looking for an experienced practitioner who believes in the power of youth work, understands the importance of positive relationships with young people, and wants to help build a skilled and confident workforce.
Our Youth Service is all about creating
“somewhere to go, something to do and someone to talk to”
for young people across the Island. This is a real chance to help shape practice across the Island while supporting staff to deliver safe, engaging and meaningful opportunities for young people.
A unique professional development opportunity
We recognise that talented professionals who work with young people come from a range of backgrounds.
We welcome applications from talented professionals who work with young people across sectors including youth work, education, social care, health, early help, inclusion, the voluntary sector, youth justice and community services.
If you hold a relevant Level 3 qualification,
have at least three years' experience working with young people, and can inspire and lead others, we'd like to hear from you.
If successful, you will be supported through a fully funded professional development pathway leading to a JNC-recognised Level 6 Youth Work qualification within three years. This investment, worth over £10,000, provides an excellent opportunity to become a professionally qualified and registered Youth Worker.
The Youth Service will provide:
Funding for Level 6 Youth Work studies
Professional mentoring and supervision
Opportunities to gain experience across a range of youth work settings
Support from experienced qualified youth work professionals
Access to national networks and training opportunities
In return, we are looking for someone committed to their own professional development and improving outcomes for young people on the Isle of Man.
Lead, develop and inspire youth work across the Island
You will provide professional leadership across the Youth Service, support colleagues to understand and deliver high-quality youth work, and promote the values, ethics and principles that sit at the heart of the profession. You will lead island-wide initiatives including:
Mobile youth provision and the Youth Bus
Detached and outreach youth work
Targeted programmes and intervention work
Youth participation and youth voice
Workforce development and training
Residentials and international youth exchanges
Partnership projects with schools, health, social care and third sector organisations
This is a varied and rewarding role where no two days are the same, combining hands-on youth work with strategic leadership of practice. You’ll help create opportunities that support young people to build confidence, develop skills and thrive in their communities.

Has at least three years’ experience working with young people
Understands relationship-based youth work
Demonstrates leadership potential
Can support and develop colleagues
Understands safeguarding responsibilities
Is committed to youth-centred practice
Values young people’s participation and voice

The Isle of Man Appointments Commission is an independent body seeking applications for the position of
Commissioner - Income Tax Commissioners
.
The Commissioners determine appeals against an assessment, charge, notice or other action of the Assessor that has been issued to a person who is aggrieved by that assessment, charge, notice or action and wishes to contest it. They also determine applications made by the Assessor of Income Tax relating to requests made under the Isle of Man’s various international agreements that provide for the exchange of information.

The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (“the Authority”) regulates firms engaged in financial activities, including insurance, pensions, banking, investments, fiduciary services, and fund administration. MANAGER – NON- LIFE INSURANCE (PRUDENTIAL SUPERVISION)
An opportunity has arisen at the Authority for the role of Manager – Non-Life Insurance in the Prudential Supervision Division. This role offers a rewarding position for the right candidate, to work as a part of diverse team supervising over 130 regulated entities and overseeing a sector that manages £5bn of policyholder assets.

Contribute to the development of the Isle of Man’s financial system, particularly the Non-Life insurance sector;
Play an important role in the delivery of the Authority’s diverse and important mandate;
Assist with the delivery of strategically important supervision work as part of a highly professional team;
Build a fulfilling career, reaching your full potential and feeling valued in an environment that supports diversity and inclusion;
Be part of a dynamic team where no two days are the same.

Job Advert
Isle of Man Mental Health Act 1998:
Second Opinion Appointed Doctors
The Department of Health and Social Care (‘the Department’) are currently seeking to add to the existing pool of Second Opinion Appointed Doctors (SOADs), with applications for the unique role being welcomed until 31 October 2026.
If you are a qualified psychiatrist with at least 5 years’ practical experience at a senior level, then this could be an opportunity for you.
About the Isle of Man
The Isle of Man is a British Crown Dependency, located in the middle of the Irish Sea. As a Crown Dependency the Isle of Man has its own government that upholds laws and regulations, with an NHS style health care system.
Whilst the island does not fall under the jurisdiction or scrutiny of the NHS and CQC, we adopt the same or similar methodology and good practice as evidenced in the UK.
The easiest routes to get to the Isle of Man are via London airports, or transport links in the Northwest (air and sea).
Mental Health
The island has its own Mental Health Act 1998 (‘the Act’), which is based on the UK’s Mental Health Act 1983.
This includes safeguards for people who are covered by the powers of the Act, which describes the responsibilities of the Responsible Medical Officer or doctor and in what circumstances a second opinion for treatment should be sought from an independent Psychiatrist (SOAD).
SOADs are appointed by the Department, however interviews are undertaken by the local Mental Health Commission.
Reporting and accountability
The SOADs will report through the Head of Quality and Compliance at the Department of Health and Social Care.
The role and requirements from applicants
The pool of SOADs registered with the Department are completely independent of local services and work as and when requested. This is generally between 4 to 6 times per year, usually for one day each time. However, you may need to see up to 3 patients per visit.
The SOADs are called upon to provide second opinions for a patient’s treatment, where that patient is covered by the powers of the Act.
To fulfil this role, you must be able to meet the following criteria:
Qualified Psychiatrist, with at 5 years’ experience of clinical practice in a senior role
General Medical Council (GMC) registered – Please include your reference number
Hold a GMC Specialist registration
Member of the Royal College of Psychiatrists or have an equivalent qualification recognised by the Royal College of Psychiatrists.
Registered in good standing for Continued Professional Development.
Knowledge and experience of the Mental Health Act 1983 (England and Wales)
Experience in working with patients in acute hospital settings.
The Department offers an excellent remuneration package which includes travel and associated expenses.
